Chapter 6: System Design & Implementation

6.1 Unified Modeling Language (UML) Modeling

Object-oriented analysis and structural modeling for AssetDesk are formalized through standard Unified Modeling Language (UML 2.5) diagrams. Figure 6.1 captures functional interactions across three distinct user roles, while Figure 6.2 models class attributes, multiplicities, and persistence associations.

Actor Roles & Boundary Scopes: Administrator exercises complete oversight (user creation, license key reveal, system configuration, audit review, CSV exports). IT Support triages hardware assets, executes state transitions, and resolves assigned support tickets. Employee accesses self-service inventory, logs tickets, participates in threaded comments, and reopens resolved tickets.
Structural Schema Entities: Details attributes and methods for User, Asset, License, Ticket, AuditLog, and Counter. Multiplicities enforce 1:N relations (User to assigned Assets and created Tickets) and N:M seat allocations (License to Users) with subdocument composition.

6.1.1 Operational Activity Workflows

Activity diagrams specify algorithmic control flow, decision branches, and swimlane handoffs across primary lifecycle workflows: authenticated session establishment, concurrency-safe hardware assignment, and incident resolution.

Validates credentials against active directory hash. Successful bcrypt comparison issues signed JWT token; failed attempts increment rate-limiter counters.
Verifies target user status, checks asset availability, executes atomic database state mutation, and persists compliance audit record.
Captures employee ticket creation with SLA calculation, technician auto/manual assignment, iterative threaded comments, resolution note validation (>= 5 chars), employee confirmation, and administrative closure.

6.1.2 Sequence & State Machine Behavioral Models

Sequence diagrams illustrate chronological message passing between client components, Express controllers, and MongoDB models. State machine diagrams govern valid status transitions.

Client POST dispatches to authController; verifies passwordHash; returns signed JWT.
Atomic findOneAndUpdate with condition guard; returns populated user object.
Validates state transition rule; enforces resolution note; timestamps resolvedAt.
Strict transitions: OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED → CLOSED. Employees may reopen resolved tickets to IN_PROGRESS; closed tickets are immutable.
Lifecycle path: AVAILABLE ↔ ASSIGNED; transition to MAINTENANCE temporarily clears assignment; terminal state is RETIRED.

6.2 Database Design & Data Dictionary (Part I)

The data architecture is implemented in MongoDB Community Edition using Mongoose schemas. Tables 6.1 through 6.3 define field specifications, BSON data types, nullability constraints, and index mappings extracted programmatically from User.js, Asset.js, and Counter.js.

Table 6.1: User Collection Schema Specification (users)
Field Name BSON Type Required Key / Index Functional Description
_id ObjectId Yes Primary Key (PK) Unique 12-byte BSON document identifier
name String Yes — Full name of user (2–100 characters, trimmed)
email String Yes Unique Index Unique lowercase email address used for login authentication
passwordHash String Yes — Bcrypt hash with 10 salt rounds (hidden from API JSON payloads)
role String No — Access control tier: ADMIN, IT_SUPPORT, EMPLOYEE
department String No — Corporate department / functional division assignment
isActive Boolean No — Operational account state flag (soft deactivation guard)
createdAt / updatedAt Date No — Mongoose automated audit timestamps for document lifecycle
Table 6.2: Asset Collection Schema Specification (assets)
Field Name BSON Type Required Key / Index Functional Description
_id ObjectId Yes Primary Key (PK) Unique 12-byte BSON document identifier
assetTag String No Unique Index Monotonic barcode tag identifier (e.g., AST-2026-0001)
serialNumber String Yes Unique Index OEM hardware serial number guaranteeing physical uniqueness
name String Yes — Hardware brand, model, and configuration descriptor
category String Yes Compound Index Enum: LAPTOP, DESKTOP, MONITOR, PRINTER, NETWORK, MOBILE, OTHER
status String No Compound Index Enum: AVAILABLE, ASSIGNED, MAINTENANCE, RETIRED
assignedTo ObjectId No FK → User Foreign key reference to allocated employee user document
purchaseDate / warranty Date No — Procurement invoice date and warranty protection expiration date
notes String No — Maintenance history, technical remarks (max 500 characters)
Table 6.3: Counter Collection Schema Specification (counters)
Field Name BSON Type Required Key / Index Functional Description
key String Yes Unique Index Sequence namespace identifier (e.g., asset-2026, ticket-2026)
seq Number No — Atomic integer sequence incremented via $inc in findOneAndUpdate

6.2.2 Data Dictionary (Part II) & Relational Mapping

Tables 6.4 through 6.6 document schemas for software license allocation, incident ticket tracking, and compliance audit logging. Table 6.7 summarizes referential integrity constraints across collections.

Table 6.4: License Collection Schema Specification (licenses)
Field Name BSON Type Required Key / Index Functional Description
softwareName / vendor String Yes — Commercial software title descriptor and publishing vendor organization
licenseKey String Yes — Volume license activation key (masked in UI for non-admins)
totalSeats Number Yes — Maximum permitted concurrent user seat entitlement quota (integer >= 1)
allocations Array<SubDoc> No FK → User Active seat assignments containing user (ObjectId) and allocatedAt
expiryDate Date Yes Index (Asc) License contract renewal date used by cron daemon for alert dispatch
Table 6.5: Ticket Collection Schema Specification (tickets)
Field Name BSON Type Required Key / Index Functional Description
ticketCode String No Unique Index Formatted incident identifier (e.g., TCK-2026-0001)
title / description String Yes — Issue summary (5–150 chars) and detailed incident explanation (max 2000 chars)
category / priority String Yes Index Category (HARDWARE, SOFTWARE, etc.) and priority (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL)
status String No Index Workflow state: OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, CLOSED
createdBy / assignedTo ObjectId Yes / No FK → User Ticket author (Employee) and assigned technician (IT_SUPPORT)
relatedAsset ObjectId No FK → Asset Optional hardware asset linked to the technical incident
comments Array<SubDoc> No FK → User Thread messages: author (User ref), message, and createdAt
dueAt / resolvedAt / closedAt Date No Index SLA resolution deadline, resolution timestamp, and administrative closure timestamp
resolutionNote String No — Mandatory technical explanation captured when status transitions to RESOLVED
Table 6.6: AuditLog Collection Schema Specification (auditlogs)
Field Name BSON Type Required Key / Index Functional Description
user / userName ObjectId / String No / Yes FK → User Actor user ID reference and immutable plaintext name snapshot
action / entity String Yes Compound Index Audit verb (LOGIN, ASSET_ASSIGN, etc.) and resource domain (AUTH, ASSET, TICKET)
entityId / details String No — Target resource identifier and JSON-serialized audit payload
ipAddress / timestamp String / Date No Index (Desc) Client IP address and immutable record creation timestamp
Table 6.7: Relational Integrity & Schema Foreign Key Mappings
Source Entity → Target Entity Cardinality Implementation Field Integrity Rule & Validation Guard
Asset → User N : 1 (Zero-or-One) Asset.assignedTo Must reference an active user; unassignment sets field to null.
Ticket → User (Creator) N : 1 Ticket.createdBy Mandatory reference to authoring employee; immutable post-creation.
Ticket → User (Technician) N : 1 (Zero-or-One) Ticket.assignedTo Must reference user with role ADMIN or IT_SUPPORT.
License → User (Seat Allocations) N : M allocations.user Seat array cannot exceed totalSeats quota constraint.

6.3 Entity-Relationship (E-R) Diagram & Indexing Strategy

The conceptual data model is expressed in Figure 6.11 as an Entity-Relationship (ER) diagram illustrating Crow’s Foot cardinalities. While MongoDB is a schema-flexible document store, strict referential integrity and performance indexing are maintained at the Mongoose ODM layer.

Entity Relationships: User serves as the central entity linked to assigned hardware (Asset), allocated software seats (License), incident requests (Ticket), and audit actions (AuditLog). Counter maintains decoupled monotonic counters for atomic code generation.
Table 6.8: Database Indexing Strategy & Performance Optimization
Collection Indexed Field(s) Index Type Operational Query Optimization Rationale
users email Unique B-Tree Provides O(1) instantaneous lookup during user login and duplicate registration guard.
assets assetTag, serialNumber Unique B-Tree Guarantees physical device tag and OEM hardware serial uniqueness across database.
assets status, category Compound Index Accelerates catalog filtering and pagination queries, maintaining avg latency <7.5ms.
licenses expiryDate Ascending Index Optimizes daily background cron scans identifying licenses expiring within 30 days.
tickets ticketCode Unique B-Tree Enables fast direct URL lookup and search by ticket identifier (e.g., TCK-2026-0001).
tickets status, priority, dueAt Compound Index Powers technician queue ordering and real-time SLA overdue highlight computation.
auditlogs timestamp (desc), entity Compound Index Supports high-throughput compliance audit review and date-range CSV reporting.

6.5 Implementation: Program Code Samples

Core business logic is encapsulated in production JavaScript modules. Below are four key code listings illustrating token authentication, concurrency guards, state machine rules, and dynamic virtual properties.

Listing 6.1: JWT Authentication Middleware (server/src/middleware/auth.js:11-30)
async function authenticate(req, res, next) { try { const authHeader = req.headers.authorization; if (!authHeader || !authHeader.startsWith("Bearer ")) { return next(ApiError.unauthorized("Authentication token required")); } const token = authHeader.split(" ")[1]; let decoded = jwt.verify(token, config.JWT_SECRET, { algorithms: ["HS256"] }); req.user = decoded; next(); } catch (err) { return next(ApiError.unauthorized(err.name === "TokenExpiredError" ? "Token expired" : "Invalid token")); } }

Explanation: Extracts Bearer tokens from authorization headers, enforces HS256 algorithm integrity, decodes user claims into req.user, and traps expiration errors.

Listing 6.2: Atomic Asset Assignment with Concurrency Guard (server/src/controllers/assets.js:256-281)
const asset = await Asset.findOneAndUpdate( { _id: req.params.id, status: "AVAILABLE" }, { $set: { status: "ASSIGNED", assignedTo: targetUser._id } }, { new: true } ).populate("assignedTo", "name email"); if (!asset) { throw ApiError.badRequest("Asset is not available or concurrently allocated"); }

Explanation: Atomic condition guard prevents double-allocation race conditions under concurrent assignment requests without requiring heavy multi-document transactions.

Listing 6.3: Ticket State Machine Transition Rules (server/src/services/ticketRules.js:14-33)
const VALID_TRANSITIONS = { OPEN: ["IN_PROGRESS"], IN_PROGRESS: ["RESOLVED"], RESOLVED: ["IN_PROGRESS", "CLOSED"], CLOSED: [] }; function canTransition(from, to) { if (!from || !to || from === to) return false; return (VALID_TRANSITIONS[from] || []).includes(to); }

Explanation: Pure deterministic transition lookup table guaranteeing that tickets progress linearly through verified states and protecting closed tickets from further mutation.

Listing 6.4: Software License Expiry & Status Virtual (server/src/models/License.js:90-104)
licenseSchema.virtual("status").get(function () { if (!this.expiryDate) return "ACTIVE"; const today = startOfToday(), expiry = new Date(this.expiryDate); if (expiry.getTime() < today.getTime()) return "EXPIRED"; if (expiry.getTime() <= addDays(today, 30).getTime()) return "EXPIRING"; return "ACTIVE"; });

Explanation: Computes dynamic status (ACTIVE, EXPIRING, EXPIRED) in real time against UTC midnight boundaries without requiring stale persisted status flags.

6.6 Implementation of Security Architecture

AssetDesk adopts a comprehensive defense-in-depth security model. Protections operate across network edge proxies, Express middleware stacks, cryptographic models, and persistence layers. Table 6.10 maps every implemented security control to its operational source file and verifying automated test case.

Table 6.10: Security Controls Implementation & Verification Traceability Matrix
Security Control Technical Implementation Mechanism Source Code Location Verified By
Salted Password Hashing One-way Bcrypt hashing with 10 salt rounds executed in Mongoose pre-save hook. server/src/models/User.js UT-06, SEC-08
Stateless Token Auth Cryptographically signed HMAC-SHA256 JWT tokens with 24-hour expiration. server/src/middleware/auth.js IT-M1-02, SEC-01
Role-Based Access Control Route-level RBAC guards enforcing ADMIN, IT_SUPPORT, or EMPLOYEE roles. server/src/middleware/roles.js IT-M1-04, SEC-02
Input Parameter Sanitation Strict validation rules checking string lengths, email regex, and integer ranges. server/src/middleware/validate.js UT-02, SEC-07
Brute-Force Rate Limiting IP-based sliding window rate limiter (max 10 login attempts per 15-minute window). server/src/middleware/rateLimiter.js SEC-04
HTTP Security Headers Helmet middleware configuring CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, and nosniff policies. server/src/app.js SEC-05
CORS Policy Enforcement Restricts cross-origin requests exclusively to whitelisted frontend origin domain. server/src/config/cors.js SEC-06
NoSQL Injection Defense Express sanitizer stripping $ and . operators alongside typed Mongoose schemas. server/src/app.js SEC-07
Sensitive Key Masking Software keys masked as ****-****-XXXX; unmasking restricted to ADMIN. server/src/controllers/licenses.js SEC-09
CSV Formula Injection Defense Prepending risky leading characters (=, +, -, @) with single quotes on export. server/src/services/csv.js UT-44, SEC-10
Tamper-Proof Audit Trail Append-only pre-hook preventing update/delete operations on AuditLog documents. server/src/models/AuditLog.js IT-M5-03, SEC-03
Transport Layer Security End-to-end HTTPS/TLS encryption configured on edge reverse proxy (NGINX/Cloud). server/src/server.js SEC-11
Security Architecture Synthesis: By integrating cryptographic token validation at the network boundary, parameterized query sanitization in application middleware, and append-only immutability in the database tier, AssetDesk achieves a robust security posture verified across 12 dedicated automated security test suites (SEC-01 through SEC-12).
